source_refs.locator: Printed p. 8, section 1.1.1, ‘Geography, climate, and socioeconomics.’

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2022-11 reports: The report associates El Niño with more flooding on the Costa and drought in the Sierra; agriculture and fisheries’ large employment and export shares add exposure.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2022-11 reports: The report says informality, inequality and low safe-water/sanitation access increase climate welfare vulnerability; 73% of employed people had informal jobs in 2019, with worker poverty rates over four times formal peers.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

geographies: Peru; regional, provincial and district levels
evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2022-11 reports: The report describes weak national–regional coordination and limited subnational DRM participation; only 13 regions, 28 provinces and 39 districts had prevention plans, while central authorities led the 2017 El Niño emergency outside the DRM framework.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: Printed pp. 24–25, Box 4.1, water-balance assessment and Map B4.1.1.

evidence.scenario: The report labels the additional-basin map RCP8.5 for 2030 and describes broader model projections for 2030 and 2050.
evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2023 reports: The diagnostic’s approximately 5-km water-balance model found deficits in 72 of 231 basins; six additional basins could enter deficit under its RCP8.5 projection.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: Printed pp. 24 and 26, Rimac Basin and northern-coast water-stress discussion.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2023 reports: The report identifies the Rimac Basin as the sharpest deficit: Lima’s 11 million residents rely on Atlantic-region transfers for several months yearly; north-coast irrigated agriculture is also threatened by scarcity.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: Printed p. 11, irrigation coverage and regional poverty discussion.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2023 reports: In Sierra and Alta Selva, where half of rural residents are poor, only about 20% of cultivated land is irrigated, leaving farming exposed to rainfall shifts; most Costa agricultural land is irrigated.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: Printed p. 25 and Annex 4, flood-risk scenario and very-high-risk district list.

evidence.scenario: Potential January–March rainfall anomalies associated with historical El Niño and La Niña episodes; a risk scenario, not a dated event forecast or climate-change projection.
evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025 reports: Under possible summer El Niño/La Niña rainfall anomalies, the plan rates 78 districts across 12 departments very high flood risk, covering 2.396 million people; Annex 4 names Belén and Piura districts including Catacaos and Tambogrande.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.
